reason: The hypothesis directly applies the surface grain refinement strategy from P5/P6 (ultrafine-grained AlCoCrFeNi) to a different alloy (HfNbTaTiZr) and proposes that the same mechanism (enhanced nucleation of protective oxides via high-density grain boundaries) will work for HfO2/ZrO2 scales. However, P5/P6 already explicitly propose this exact transfer as future work, stating that surface deformation techniques have been studied for oxidation behavior and that the approach should be extended to other systems. The hypothesis merely executes that proposed future work without adding a new mechanistic insight, combination of findings, or resolution of a conflict. The mechanical property targets are taken directly from the known properties of HfNbTaTiZr (P4, P12, P14).
copied_elements: surface mechanical treatment (shot peening/UNSM) to create ultrafine-grained surface layer
ultrafine grains increase nucleation density of protective oxides and limit fast diffusion paths
dense, adherent oxide scale acts as diffusion barrier
improved oxidation resistance (lower weight gain) while retaining bulk mechanical properties
baseline untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr with poor oxidation resistance
falsification test design (treated vs. untreated, oxidation exposure, mechanical testing)
